correctness.rationale: For d≥2 and continuous positive κ, the two published densities κ^a/I_a and κ^b/I_b define probabilities with a+b=1. Substitution gives H²=1−I_1/2/√(I_aI_b). Cauchy–Schwarz and equality show vanishing iff constant curvature (hence ball). F=log I_t has Fʺ(t)=Var_{μ_t}(logκ); the elementary midpoint Green-kernel identity proves −log(1−H²)=1/2∫_a^b min(t−a,b−t)Fʺ(t)dt. Similarity exponent cancellation and boundary d≥2 checked. Independent three finite weighted-curvature analogues corroborate midpoint variance, not an infinite-body proof.

originality.rationale: FAIL: two primary source results together already imply the entire claim by direct specialization. Hoehner specifies a=1/(d+1),b=d/(d+1) and ball rigidity; Nielsen 2024 Proposition 4 proves for ANY exponential family pθ∝exp(θT−F(θ)) the Bhattacharyya coefficient ρ=exp(−J_F(a,b)); set T=log κ and α=1/2. This is EXACTLY I_1/2/√(I_a I_b), with H²=1−ρ. Its variance integral is the ordinary midpoint second-derivative integration of the same Jensen gap and no model-specific new estimate. The original geometric formula is a direct corollary/renaming, regardless of absence of its exact wording.
